rows.en:
...The school gate was almost in reach.
If I can just get that far, I'll be safe for sure...
Just a little farther...
Almost there...!
The instant that thought crossed his mind...
"Whoa!"{p}

Nanase tripped over something and went down.
When he looked, a hand sprouting from the ground had a firm grip on his ankle.
"Let go!"
Nanase struggled desperately to shake the hand off.
The ghosts were already closing in.
...If he didn't get away fast, they would take him with them!

...And just then.
Light swept over everything around him.{p}

..........Dawn had broken.
And then, as if melting into the morning sun, the ghosts faded away.
...Am I saved?
Thank... goodness..........
And with that, he passed out.
...In that very instant,
"Aww, we were so close..."
he heard a shrill voice, like a child's. Or so he says.{p}

After that...
Nanase was found lying unconscious by a student arriving for school, and he was saved.
But you know, when they helped him up, his body was covered in bruises.
Reddish-purple handprints were plastered all over him, they say.
For a while, he suffered from those bruises and aching joints.
Still, he ought to be grateful just to have escaped with his life.
Perhaps his survival really was close to a miracle.
If the sun had come up even one second later that morning, I don't think Nanase would have made it.{p}

Heh, there are quite a lot of them, you know.
People who go missing at school after hours...
...Say, {a}.
Now you understand why I said school after hours is dangerous, don't you?
Until dawn breaks, the school is a place where the dead study.
Any living person who wanders in is made one of them, without being given a say.
After all, the more friends you have, the less lonely you are.
Heh heh heh...
That is the end of my story.{p}

Oh my, look at the time already.
...It's the witching hour.
And we've only just finished the second story...
Heh...{p}

None of us can escape now, can we?
The seven wonders have only just begun...
Next is the third story.
I wonder who will tell it...?{p}

Right around that time...
Nanase had gone to the make-up class and still hadn't come home, so there was a bit of an uproar at his house.
No matter how many times they called the school, no one answered.
Even if the make-up class was already over, the teacher on night duty should have been there.
(Maybe I should call the police...?)
Just as his worried mother was starting to think that...
"I'm home."
A voice came from the front door.
...It was Nanase's voice.
"Welcome home...
You're late, aren't you?"
Relieved, his mother went out to the entryway to meet him.
But...
There was no one at the door.

"Yasuhiro...?"
His mother went outside to look for him.
But Nanase was nowhere to be seen.
"Yasuhiro...?
Where are you?"
His mother called his name once more.
And then,
"Oh no!
I forgot it...☆"
she heard Nanase say, sounding flustered, or so they say.
After that, the voice cut off without a trace.{p}
At that very moment, the phone in Nanase's house rang.
The call was from the hospital.{p}

Heh heh heh...
When he said, back then,
"I forgot it,"
he meant his own body, didn't he?
Honestly... what a forgetful little thing he is.{p}

Oh, yes...
Here's the strange part.
There was no midnight make-up class that day.
And the school said it had never contacted Nanase's family about one, either...
...Say, {a}.
Now you understand why I said school after hours is dangerous, don't you?
Until dawn breaks, the school is a place where the dead study.
Any living person who wanders in is made one of them, without being given a say.
After all, the more friends you have, the less lonely you are.{p}

Heh heh heh...
But it really was a shame about Nanase.
I was sure he'd make a good friend...
To think someone would happen by just when we were so close...
...Oh?
I said something odd just now, didn't I?
Heh, I'm only joking.
Don't let it bother you...{p}

I simply thought that's how the students of the ghost classroom must feel.
You were startled, weren't you?
...I'm sorry.
Somehow, I think I understand them.
A lazybones like Nanase, who gives up on his homework just because he forgot something... To the ghost classroom's students, who keep on studying even after death, someone like that is simply unforgivable.{p}

...Heh, don't you think so?
Oh, come to think of it, you're a bit of a lazybones yourself, aren't you, {a}?
Heh heh heh...
Little Miss Lazybonesina.
I think we could become good friends, you and I...

...Tell me, isn't living a bother too?
You don't need a life like that, do you...?
Oh, are you frightened?
You really are fun to watch, you know.
Heh heh heh...

It was all just my joke.
Let's leave it at that...
All right?
And there's no need to worry about the seven wonders.
Look, it's already the witching hour.
We've only just finished the second story...
No one can say whether we'll all still be safe by the time the seventh story ends...
Next is the third story.
I wonder who will tell it...?{p}
Oh, you've never been inside?{p}

Heh heh...
It is off-limits, after all.
Though it seems a few of the people here have been there...
Oh my, some of you look frightened.
Don't worry...
I won't say a word about any of you to the teachers.
I never tell lies.{p}
Oh, you've never been inside?{p}

Heh heh...
It is off-limits, after all.
Though it seems a few of the people here have been there...
Oh my, some of you look frightened.
Don't worry...
I won't say a word about any of you to the teachers.
I never tell lies.{p}
...Now, back to the story.{p}

Nanase headed for the art room.
"No sweat, no sweat.
I'm not scared one bit."
That's what he kept telling himself, you see.{p}

Through the dark, lonely hallway, down the stairs, along the walkway...
He reached the old school building without incident.{p}

The art room was at the far end of the second floor...
He was nearly there.
But then...
"..........?"{p}

Late at night as it was, there was a classroom with its lights on.
...Class going on at this hour?
Or...
Maybe someone else came back for something they forgot, same as me...?
Nanase crept toward the lit classroom, muffling his footsteps.{p}

Really...?
How surprising.
I thought you'd be more of a coward.
Like Nanase...{p}

I'm scared...☆
The instant he thought it, he spun around and broke into a run.
He wasn't thinking about his homework anymore.
All he could think about, over and over, was running for his life.
...But you know.
Whether you call it bad luck or simply the obvious outcome...
"Waaah!"{p}
Running blindly through the dark, he caught his foot on one of the walkway boards and fell flat.

Clatter... clunk...
Suddenly he heard a dull sound right behind him.
When he fearfully turned around...
"..........☆"
Nanase couldn't help gasping.{p}

What came out from the far end of the walkway was a soldier in a tattered military uniform.
The soldier was pushing an empty cart, staring into space with exhausted, hollow eyes.
Then the soldier stopped in front of Nanase, who was shaking all over, and those hollow eyes flashed with a fierce glint, glaring at him with a terrifying face.

Nanase ran for his life.
The door to the new school building was right in front of him.{p}

That's right.
Nanase ran up the stairs and fled to the second floor.
He figured no one could climb stairs while pushing a cart.
Heh, a clever idea, don't you think?{p}

...But you know.
That sort of logic doesn't work on ghosts.
Clatter... clunk...
With that dull sound echoing, the soldier came calmly up the stairs.
Still pushing the cart, of course...
Nanase was getting tired, so he was the one at a disadvantage.
...At this rate, I'm going to get caught!{p}
With that thought, Nanase ducked into the nearest classroom and decided to hide under a desk without moving a muscle.{p}
..........Surprisingly, that's exactly what happened.{p}

"Waaaaaah☆"
With a single yell, Nanase charged straight at the cart the soldier was pushing.
I can only think he'd lost all sense out of desperation.
Or was he planning to knock the soldier down?
At any rate, Nanase rammed right into the cart.
I'm going to hit it...☆
The instant he thought that, the cart and the soldier both vanished as if wiped away.{p}

Thud...!
Carried by his own momentum, Nanase fell sprawling onto the hallway floor.{p}

And then his vision was flooded with red.
The smell of blood hung heavy in the air.
...Oh, so I'm going to die.
I'm losing this much blood, but nothing hurts at all.
I guess I've gone numb...
That's what Nanase was thinking as he slowly closed his eyes, they say.
He was sure he would simply black out and die.
But...
No matter how long he waited, the moment of death never came.
Far from blacking out, his head was growing clear and sharp, and when he felt along his body with his hands, there was nothing like an injury anywhere...
...Then what is this red liquid?
The slimy feel of it, that peculiar smell... I was so sure it was blood...
Nanase just sat there on the floor, dazed.{p}

The one who found him like that was the teacher on night duty, making the rounds.
"Who's there, at this time of night...☆"
Heh...
The teacher must have been shocked.
After all, there was a student covered in blood, huddled in the hallway of the old school building.
"What on earth were you doing to end up like this★"
"Well, you see.........."
After hearing Nanase's story, the teacher made a sour face and muttered under their breath,
"Not again..."
...just like that.{p}

Heh, the truth is...
Around that time, there had been frequent incidents of the cart being taken out of the storage shed.
The shed door was shut and the lock was fastened, and yet the cart kept inside would be gone.
If you followed the ruts it left behind, you'd find the cart abandoned in a corner of the schoolyard, after being dragged all over the place.
You know the cherry tree behind the old school building, don't you?
I hear it was around there.
The teachers seemed to think it was just someone's prank.
But if Nanase's story is true, then it was all the work of the soldier's ghost, wasn't it?
Oh, yes...
The next morning, the cart was found lying at the foot of the cherry tree.
They say the cart bed was covered in a spreading stain, like the traces of blood... or maybe it wasn't.{p}

Heh heh...
Are you sure you should be saying that?{p}

You've been inside the old school building, haven't you?
If you want me to keep it a secret from the teachers, you'll come along and see it with us.{p}All right?
I don't mind going
I don't want to go

Heh...
You should have said so from the start.{p}

But...
If you want to get through your school life here safely, that may be for the best.
A wise person keeps away from danger... as the saying goes.
...Well then, that brings my story to an end.{p}

Oh...
Isn't it nearly the witching hour by now?
But no one can escape, can they?
We've only just finished the second story...
The seven wonders have barely begun...
Now, whose turn is next, I wonder...?{p}

"Okay, then we'll head back first.
...Please hurry back, all right?"
"Yes...
I know. I'll be fine."{p}

...Partly because it was cloudy, it was pretty dim outside.
Without anyone saying a word, we all stopped and looked back at the old school building...
The old school building, which was finally going to be torn down.
It was an eerie place even in broad daylight, and now, at dusk like this, Iwashita was in there all alone...
"Hey...
Ain't it dangerous for a girl to be all alone in a place like that?"
someone murmured...
"It's the perfect place for a burglar or someone to sneak into, after all."
"A few years back, there was that case where an escaped convict was hiding in a gym storeroom, and a student who went in without knowing got killed, right?
Which school was that again...?"{p}

...Hmm.
When they say things like that, I start to feel worried.
What if Iwashita is in danger...
...Should I go back to the old school building?
The instant I thought that...{p}

"Eeeeeeeeek☆"
A horrific scream rang out.
What met our eyes as we rushed into the old school building was a cart moving away down the dim hallway, and a soldier in military uniform.
But the soldier and the cart soon vanished into the darkness...{p}

...Where's Iwashita?
Where is she★
"Hey, look at this.
...It's blood."{p}

...It's true.
There were drops of blood all along the hallway floor.
Leading right into the darkness where the soldier had vanished...
Could it be... Iwashita's...★
If someone was being carried on that cart, then it must have been...☆
"Is she... dead?"
one of the members suddenly murmured.

As if those words had set it off, tension shot through all of us.
"She must be.
It was only for a second, but you all saw the soldier's ghost too, didn't you?
That was the soldier's ghost from her story, no doubt about it!
She was killed by the soldier's ghost!"
"I-it's not my fault."
"Don't look at me, either.
It's the fault of whoever said to leave her and go back!"
...What?!
You're saying this is all my fault★
"Anyway, let's go get a teacher."
...Ah, everyone, wait!
Don't leave me behind...☆
Clunk...
A dull sound echoed behind me.{p}

When I turned around, there stood Iwashita, her face deathly pale...
Iwashita was smiling eerily, bright red blood dripping from her lips.
And then... she murmured just a few words.
"There's one more cart, you know..."{p}
"No, I'll wait for Iwashita."{p}
